data.title: Dutasteride
data.summary: VIII Antiandrogen · Dual 5α-reductase inhibitor (types I and II)
data.body:
_Oral · VIII Antiandrogen_

**Class:** Dual 5α-reductase inhibitor (types I and II)

## Mechanism of action
- Inhibits both type I (sebaceous glands, skin) and type II (hair follicle, prostate) 5α-reductase
- Lowers serum DHT by more than 90% — more than finasteride

## Pharmacokinetics
- Very long half-life (about 5 weeks); effect persists for months after stopping
- Metabolised by CYP3A4

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Male androgenetic alopecia (approved in Korea/Japan at 0.5 mg; off-label elsewhere) — slightly more effective than finasteride
- Female pattern hair loss in post-menopausal women (off-label)
- Mesotherapy (intradermal dutasteride) for AGA
- Benign prostatic hyperplasia

## Dose & formulations
- 0.5 mg once daily (some use 0.5 mg 2–3 times a week); soft capsules should not be opened

## Adverse effects
- Sexual side effects (similar to or slightly more than finasteride)
- Gynaecomastia, breast tenderness
- PSA lowered by about 50%

## Contraindications
- Women of childbearing potential and pregnancy; children
- Men should not donate blood for 6 months after the last dose (long half-life)

## Drug interactions
- Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (ritonavir, ketoconazole) raise levels

## Monitoring
- Baseline PSA in older men

## Pregnancy & lactation
Contraindicated (old FDA category X). Pregnant women should not handle leaking capsules.

## Viva points
- Blocks both isoenzymes — more DHT suppression than finasteride
- Very long half-life — no blood donation for 6 months after stopping

_Sources: Wolverton 4e ch.34; Khopkar (Miscellaneous agents). Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
